recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Foundation layer. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums in shared/types are needed by every other module. Employee module has zero dependencies on other domain modules and is needed by leave for manager lookups and active-status checks.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared/types and policy. Owns balance lifecycle: initialization from policy, deduction on approval, restoration on cancellation/rejection. Must exist before leave-request can enforce balance-sufficiency checks.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared/types. Defines leave policy rules (entitlement, accrual, notice periods). Balance module needs policy to initialize balances; leave-request needs policy for validation (minimum notice, requiresManagerApproval).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Audit module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared/types. Records all state-changing operations per GP-002. Must exist before leave-request so approval/rejection/submission actions can write audit records.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Leave module (core)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior modules: shared/types, employee, policy, balance, audit. Implements the core leave-request workflow: submit, approve, reject, cancel, list, calendar. This is the largest phase — the leave service orchestrates policy validation, balance checks, employee lookups, and audit recording.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes/controllers in leave module), application (service interfaces + implementations in each module), domain (entities, value objects, repository interfaces in each module), infrastructure (repository implementations, DB connection in src/shared/db/). Dependencies flow inward: leave → {employee, policy, balance, audit} → shared/types. No circular dependencies — verified: employee and policy depend only on shared/types; balance depends on shared/types + policy; audit depends only on shared/types; leave depends on all four domain modules + shared/types. Shared value types (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, BaseEntity) placed in src/shared/types/ per the mechanical rule — they are pure data shapes with no owned business logic used by multiple modules. The leave module owns its controller and routes (API surface); other modules are pure domain/service layers with no API surface of their own.

open_questions.question: How should remainingDays be computed — as a derived field (totalEntitlement - usedDays) or as a stored column that is updated on every deduction/restoration?
open_questions.impact: Affects Balance entity design, BalanceService.recalculateBalance semantics, and data consistency guarantees. If derived, remainingDays is always consistent but requires computation on every read. If stored, reads are fast but every mutation must update it atomically.
candidate_options: Derived: remainingDays computed at query time from totalEntitlement - usedDays
Stored: remainingDays persisted and updated transactionally on every deduction/restoration
Hybrid: stored column with a recalculateBalance method that recomputes and persists, called after bulk operations

open_questions.question: What are the fiscal-year boundary rules for balance carry-over and accrual? Should unused days carry over to the next fiscal year, and if so, up to what cap?
open_questions.impact: Affects BalanceService.initializeBalance and recalculateBalance. The carry-over rule determines whether remainingDays at fiscal-year end are added to the next year's entitlement. Without this, balance initialization for a new fiscal year is underspecified.
candidate_options: No carry-over: balances reset to policy entitlement each fiscal year
Full carry-over: all remaining days carry forward, capped at maxAccumulation from policy
Partial carry-over: a configurable percentage or fixed number of days carry forward

auth_contract: Authenticated request shape: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole }. UserRole enum: 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. Identity obtained via JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route guard at the Fastify route level, never inline in service methods. Leave endpoints: submit/cancel → employee; approve/reject/listTeam → manager; policy CRUD → hr_admin; listOwn → employee.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string; details?: unknown }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code: VALIDATION_ERROR). Authentication failure → HTTP 401 (code: UNAUTHORIZED). Authorization failure → HTTP 403 (code: FORBIDDEN). Not found → HTTP 404 (code: NOT_FOUND). Conflict (e.g. overlapping leave, insufficient balance) → HTTP 409 (code: CONFLICT).
